verses.zh: 「你要爱耶和华―你的　神，常守他的吩咐、律例、典章、诫命。
verses.en: You must love the Lord your God and do what he requires; keep his statutes, ordinances, and commandments[NOTE:1] at all times.
notes: This collocation of technical terms for elements of the covenant text lends support to its importance and also signals a new section of paraenesis in which Moses will exhort Israel to covenant obedience. The Hebrew term מִשְׁמָרוֹת (mishmarot, “obligations”) sums up the three terms that follow—חֻקֹּת (khuqot), מִשְׁפָּטִים (mishpatim), and מִצְוֹת (mitsvot).
verses.commentary:
11:1 Notice how the two VERBS of this verse are related. They are theologically parallel. One
should result in the other!

- "love the Lord" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PERFECT with waw,
cf. Deut. 11:13,22. See full note at Deut. 5:10.

- "keep His charge" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

This is a repeat of Deut. 6:2,4-5; 10:12. Love is both an action (obedience) and a feeling ("with all your
heart and with all your soul and with all your might," cf. Deut. 6:5; 13:3)

▣ "His charge, His statutes, His ordinances and His commandments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

verses.zh: 你们今日当知道，我本不是和你们的儿女说话；因为他们不知道，也没有看见耶和华―你们　神的管教、威严、大能的手，和伸出来的膀臂，
verses.en: Bear in mind today that I am not speaking[NOTE:1] to your children who have not personally experienced the judgments[NOTE:2] of the Lord your God, which revealed[NOTE:3] his greatness, strength, and power.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “that not.” The words “I am speaking” have been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

Heb “who have not known and who have not seen the discipline of the Lord.” The collocation of the verbs “know” and “see” indicates that personal experience (knowing by seeing) is in view. The term translated “discipline” (KJV, ASV “chastisement”) may also be rendered “instruction,” but vv. 2b-6 indicate that the referent of the term is the various acts of divine judgment the Israelites had witnessed.

The words “which revealed” have been supplied in the translation to show the logical relationship between the terms that follow and the divine judgments. In the Hebrew text the former are in apposition to the latter.
Heb “his strong hand and his stretched-out arm.”
verses.commentary:
11:2 "And know this day that I am not speaking with your sons who have not known and who have not seen" Moses
is appealing to those who were eye witnesses ( as Levites and children under the age of military service, below 20 years old,
cf. Deut. 1:6,9,14; 5:2,5; 11:2,7) to the events of the Exodus and wilderness wanderings (cf. Deut. 4:34; 7:19).

▣ "Know" See full note at Deut. 4:35 and SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW.

▣ "the discipline of the Lord" YHWH's discipline (BDB 416) is positive, Deut. 11:3; and negative,
Deut. 11:6. Child training is a characteristic of our father God (cf. Heb. 12:5-13). This is another wisdom term
used so often in Proverbs.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "His greatness" See notes at Deut. 10:17 and 4:31.

▣ "His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm" This is an anthropomorphic phrase used for
God's power (cf. Deut. 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 9:29). See note at Deut. 4:34 and
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

verses.zh: 并他在埃及中向埃及王法老和其全地所行的神迹奇事；
verses.en: They did not see[NOTE:1] the awesome deeds he performed[NOTE:2] in the midst of Egypt against Pharaoh king of Egypt and his whole land,
notes: In the Hebrew text vv. 2-7 are one long sentence. For stylistic reasons the English translation divides the passage into three sentences. To facilitate this stylistic decision the words “They did not see” are supplied at the beginning of both v. 3 and v. 5, and “I am speaking” at the beginning of v. 7.

Heb “his signs and his deeds which he did” (NRSV similar). The collocation of “signs” and “deeds” indicates that these acts were intended to make an impression on observers and reveal something about God’s power (cf. v. 2b). The word “awesome” has been employed to bring out the force of the word “signs” in this context.

verses.zh: 也没有看见他怎样待埃及的军兵、车马，他们追赶你们的时候，耶和华怎样使红海的水淹没他们，将他们灭绝，直到今日，
verses.en: or what he did to the army of Egypt, including their horses and chariots, when he made the waters of the Red Sea[NOTE:1] overwhelm them while they were pursuing you and he[NOTE:2] annihilated them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Reed Sea.” “Reed Sea” (or “Sea of Reeds”) is a more accurate rendering of the Hebrew expression יָם סוּף (yam suf), traditionally translated “Red Sea.” See note on the term “Red Sea” in Exod 13:18.
Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “and the Lord destroyed them to this day” (cf. NRSV); NLT “he has kept them devastated to this very day.” The translation uses the verb “annihilated” to indicate the permanency of the action.
verses.commentary:
11:4 "horses and chariots" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS

▣ "Red Sea to engulf them" The Hebrew word here is "Reed Sea" (BDB 410 CONSTRUCT
BDB 693 I).

"Engulf" is literally "flow over their faces" (BDB 847, KB 1012, Hiphil PERFECT,
cf. Exod. 14:23-31), which is imagery for drowning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE RED SEA

▣

NASB
"completely destroyed them"

NKJV, NJB, Peshitta
"destroyed them to this day"

NRSV, JPSOA
"destroyed them once and for all"

REB
"destroyed them, and so things remain to this day"

LXX
"destroyed them to this very day"

The MT has the VERB "destroyed" (BDB 1, KB 2, Piel IMPERFECT
with waw plus the idiomatic phrase "to this day," which denotes a compete destruction whose consequences remain.

verses.zh: 并他在旷野怎样待你们，以致你们来到这地方；
verses.en: They did not see[NOTE:1] what he did to you in the wilderness before you reached this place,
notes: See note on these same words in v. 3.
verses.commentary: 11:5 This is a reminder of YHWH's supernatural provisions during the wilderness wanderings. See full note at Deut. 8:4.

verses.zh: 也没有看见他怎样待流便子孙以利押的儿子大坍、亚比兰，地怎样在以色列人中间开口，吞了他们和他们的家眷，并帐棚与跟他们的一切活物。
verses.en: or what he did to Dathan and Abiram,[NOTE:1] sons of Eliab the Reubenite,[NOTE:2] when the earth opened its mouth in the middle of the Israelite camp[NOTE:3] and swallowed them, their families,[NOTE:4] their tents, and all the property they brought with them.[NOTE:5]
notes: Dathan and Abiram. These two (along with others) had challenged Moses’ leadership in the desert with the result that the earth beneath them opened up and they and their families disappeared (Num 16:1-3, 31-35).
Or “the descendant of Reuben”; Heb “son of Reuben.”

Heb “in the midst of all Israel” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV); NASB “among all Israel.” In the Hebrew text these words appear at the end of the verse, but they are logically connected with the verbs. To make this clear the translation places the phrase after the first verb.
Heb “their houses,” referring to all who lived in their household. Cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “households.”
Heb “and all the substance which was at their feet.”
verses.commentary:
11:6 "Dathan and Abiram" See Numbers 16:1-35; 26:9-10; Ps. 106:16-18.

▣ "among all Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

verses.zh: 惟有你们亲眼看见耶和华所做的一切大事。」
verses.en: I am speaking to you[NOTE:1] because you are the ones who saw with your own eyes all the great deeds of the Lord.
notes: On the addition of these words in the translation see note on “They did not see” in v. 3.

verses.zh: 「所以，你们要守我今日所吩咐的一切诫命，使你们胆壮，能以进去，得你们所要得的那地，
verses.en: Now pay attention to all the commandments[NOTE:1] I am giving[NOTE:2] you today, so that you may be strong enough to enter and possess the land where you are headed,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the commandment.” The singular מִצְוָה (mitsvah, “commandment”) speaks here as elsewhere of the whole corpus of covenant stipulations in Deuteronomy (cf. 6:1, 25; 7:11; 8:1).
Heb “commanding” (so NASB, NRSV). For stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy, “giving” has been used in the translation (likewise in vv. 13, 27).
Heb “which you are crossing over there to possess it.”
verses.commentary:
11:8 "therefore" This refers to all preceding historical allusions of chapter 11 or possibly even farther
back. Much of Deuteronomy, up to this point, has rehearsed again and again the same admonitions.

▣ "possess the land" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

verses.zh: 并使你们的日子在耶和华向你们列祖起誓、应许给他们和他们后裔的地上得以长久；那是流奶与蜜之地。
verses.en: and that you may enjoy long life in the land the Lord promised to give to your ancestors[NOTE:1] and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in v. 21).
verses.commentary:
11:9 "so that you may prolong your days on the land" Compare Deut. 11:21 with Deut. 5:16. This is not an
individual promise of longevity but a cultural promise of stability to a society which honors the Law of God (cf. Deut. 4:1; 8:1)
and thereby honors the family (cf. Deut. 4:40; 5:16,33; 6:2). See full note at Deut. 4:40.

▣ "the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS.

▣ "a land flowing with milk and honey" This is not only a physical description but a technical
designation for the land of Palestine in Ugaritic, Assyrian, and Egyptian documents. See full note at Deut. 6:3.

verses.zh: 你要进去得为业的那地，本不像你出来的埃及地。你在那里撒种，用脚浇灌，像浇灌菜园一样。
verses.en: For the land where you are headed[NOTE:1] is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, a land where you planted seed and which you irrigated by hand[NOTE:2] like a vegetable garden.
notes: Heb “you are going there to possess it”; NASB “into which you are about to cross to possess it”; NRSV “that you are crossing over to occupy.”

Heb “with your foot” (so NASB, NLT). There is a two-fold significance to this phrase. First, Egypt had no rain so water supply depended on human efforts at irrigation. Second, the Nile was the source of irrigation waters but those waters sometimes had to be pumped into fields and gardens by foot-power, perhaps the kind of machinery (Arabic shaduf) still used by Egyptian farmers (see C. Aldred, The Egyptians, 181). Nevertheless, the translation uses “by hand,” since that expression is the more common English idiom for an activity performed by manual labor.
verses.commentary:
11:10 "not like the land of Egypt" The cultivation of crops was quite different in Egypt than Palestine. Palestine
had seasonal rain (cf. v. 11), Egypt had to depend on irrigation from the Nile and its annual flood.

▣ "water it with your foot" This probably refers to

- an irrigation system in which a field was flooded and then the foot was used to punch a hole in the
dike to let water out

- a treadmill used to lift water for irrigation

verses.zh: 你们要过去得为业的那地乃是有山有谷、雨水滋润之地，
verses.en: Instead, the land you are crossing the Jordan to occupy[NOTE:1] is one of hills and valleys, a land that drinks in water from the rains,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “which you are crossing over there to possess it.”
Heb “rain of heaven.”
verses.commentary:
11:11 "the land. . .drinks water from the rain of heaven" For desert peoples there is no greater blessing than
adequate, regular water (cf. Deut. 8:7-9). This good land is conditional on covenant obedience (cf. Deut. 11:16-17;
Lev. 26:14-20; Deut. 28:12,23-24; 1 Kgs. 8:35; 17:1; 2 Chr. 7:11-14; Isa. 5:6; Jer. 14; Amos 4:7-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

verses.zh: 是耶和华―你　神所眷顾的；从岁首到年终，耶和华―你　神的眼目时常看顾那地。
verses.en: a land the Lord your God looks after.[NOTE:1] He is constantly attentive to it[NOTE:2] from the beginning to the end of the year.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “seeks.” The statement reflects the ancient belief that God (Baal in Canaanite thinking) directly controlled storms and rainfall.

Constantly attentive to it. This attention to the land by the Lord is understandable in light of the centrality of the land in the Abrahamic covenant (cf. Gen 12:1, 7; 13:15; 15:7, 16, 18; 17:8; 26:3).tn Heb “the eyes of the Lord your God are continually on it” (so NIV); NASB, NRSV “always on it.”

From the beginning to the end of the year. This refers to the agricultural year that was marked by the onset of the heavy rains, thus the autumn. See note on the phrase “the former and the latter rains” in v. 14.
verses.commentary:
11:12 "the eyes of the Lord" This is an anthropomorphic description of the
Lord like Deut. 11:2. It expresses His special care and presence in the Promised Land.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism).

verses.zh: 「你们若留意听从我今日所吩咐的诫命，爱耶和华―你们的　神，尽心尽性事奉他，
verses.en: Now, if you pay close attention[NOTE:1] to my commandments that I am giving you today and love[NOTE:2] the Lord your God and serve him with all your mind and being,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “if hearing, you will hear.” The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute to emphasize the verbal idea. The translation renders this emphasis with the word “close.”
Again, the Hebrew term אָהֵב (ʾahev) draws attention to the reciprocation of divine love as a condition or sign of covenant loyalty (cf. Deut 6:5).
Heb “heart and soul” or “heart and being.” See note on the word “being” in Deut 6:5.
verses.commentary:
11:13 Notice the conditional ("if" BDB 49, cf. Deut. 11:22; and "obey" BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT from the same root, which shows emphasis
and means "to hear so as to do!") nature of YHWH's blessing is:

- "to love" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- "to serve" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT. In Arabic this root means
to worship and obey God, cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:3; 7:16; 8:1

- "with all your heart and all your soul," cf. Deut. 4:29; 6:5; and especially 10:12.

Moses is repeating this exhortation which he heard from YHWH again and again for emphasis.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "heart" For the ancient Hebrew the "heart" stood for the mind and intent, the intellect and motive of an individual.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "soul" This word means "the life force given by God" (BDB 659). It can refer to humans or animals in Genesis. See
note online at Gen. 35:18 and Lev. 17:11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 他（原文是我）必按时降秋雨春雨在你们的地上，使你们可以收藏五谷、新酒，和油，
verses.en: then he promises,[NOTE:1] “I will send rain for your land[NOTE:2] in its season, the autumn and the spring rains,[NOTE:3] so that you may gather in your grain, new wine, and olive oil.
notes: The words “he promises” do not appear in the Hebrew text but are needed in the translation to facilitate the transition from the condition (v. 13) to the promise and make it clear that the Lord is speaking the words of vv. 14-15.
Heb “the rain of your land.” In this case the genitive (modifying term) indicates the recipient of the rain.

The autumn and the spring rains. The “former” (יוֹרֶה, yoreh) and “latter” (מַלְקוֹשׁ, malqosh) rains come in abundance respectively in September/October and March/April. Planting of most crops takes place before the former rains fall and the harvests follow the latter rains.
verses.commentary:
11:14 "He will give the rain" "He will give" (BDB 678, KB 733) describes YHWH's covenant blessings and cursings
(i.e. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28):

- Deut. 11:9 ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (blessing)

- Deut. 11:14 ‒ Qal PERFECT (blessing)

- Deut. 11:15 ‒ Qal PERFECT (blessing)

- Deut. 11:17 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (curse)

- Deut. 11:17 ‒ Qal PARTICIIPLE (curse)

- Deut. 11:21 ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (blessing)

- Deut. 11:25 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (blessing)

- Deut. 11:26 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing/curse)

- Deut. 11:29 ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw (blessing/curse)

- Deut. 11:31 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing)

- Deut. 11:32 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing/curse)

YHWH wants to bless, but Israel's covenant obedience determines which response (blessing
or cursing, cf. chapters 27-29) she receives (cf. Leviticus 26).

YHWH is separate from nature yet is in control of it. He uses it to reveal Himself to
mankind (cf. Deut. 27-28; Ps. 19:1-6; Rom. 1:19-25; 2:14-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "early" Palestine has two annual times of rainfall. The early rains (for planting) come in October ‒ November
(BDB 435, cf. Jer. 5:24; Hosea 6:2; Joel 2:23).

▣ "late rains" The late rains (for maturing crops) come in February ‒ April (BDB 545, cf. Jer. 3:3; Joel 2:23). At
other times heavy dew is the only source of moisture. Hosea 6:3 uses this as imagery for end-time spiritual renewal.

▣ "your grain and your new wine and your oil" These were staples of their diet (cf. Deut. 7:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

verses.zh: 也必使你吃得饱足，并使田野为你的牲畜长草。
verses.en: I will provide pasture[NOTE:1] for your livestock and you will eat your fill.”
notes: Heb “grass in your field.”
verses.commentary:
11:15 "for your cattle" This term "cattle" (BDB 96) refers to:

- all living creatures other than humans, Gen. 8:1; Exod. 9:9,10,22

- domestic animals, Gen. 47:17; Exod. 20:10; Lev. 19:19; 26:22; Num. 3:41,45; Deut. 2:35

▣ "you shall eat and be satisfied" This VERB is a recurrent promise in Deuteronomy
(cf. Deut. 6:11; 8:10; 11:15; 14:29). It is made up of two VERBS:

- "eat" ‒ BDB 37, KB 46, Qal PERFECT with waw

- "be satisfied" ‒ BDB 959, KB 1302, Qal PERFECT with waw

verses.zh: 你们要谨慎，免得心中受迷惑，就偏离正路，去事奉敬拜别神。
verses.en: Make sure you do not turn away to serve and worship other gods![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Watch yourselves lest your heart turns and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.”
verses.commentary:
11:16-17 These verses are a warning ("beware," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE,
cf. Deut. 4:9,15,23; 6:12; 8:11; 11:16; 12:13,19,28,30; 15:9; 24:8, see note at Deut. 6:12) about idolatry and its consequences.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 耶和华的怒气向你们发作，就使天闭塞不下雨，地也不出产，使你们在耶和华所赐给你们的美地上速速灭亡。
verses.en: Then the anger of the Lord will erupt[NOTE:1] against you, and he will close up the sky[NOTE:2] so that it does not rain. The land will not yield its produce, and you will soon be removed[NOTE:3] from the good land that the Lord is about to give you.
notes: Heb “will become hot”; KJV, NASB, NRSV “will be kindled”; NAB “will flare up”; NIV, NLT “will burn.”
Or “heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
Or “be destroyed”; NAB, NIV “will soon perish.”

verses.zh: 「你们要将我这话存在心内，留在意中，系在手上为记号，戴在额上为经文；
verses.en: Fix these words of mine into your mind and being,[NOTE:1] tie them as a reminder on your hands, and let them be symbols[NOTE:2] on your forehead.
notes: Heb “heart and soul” or “heart and being.” See note on the word “being” in Deut 6:5.
On the Hebrew term טוֹטָפֹת (totafot, “reminders”), cf. Deut 6:4-9.
verses.commentary:
11:18-20 These verses are a recapitulation of Deut. 6:6-9. They are meant to impress on the faithful
the need to live life in light of God's words!

▣ "You shall therefore impress these words" This is imagery, BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal PERFECT
with waw, cf. Deut. 32:46. This is what the imagery of Deut. 6:8 and Exod. 13:9,16 means. Always keep God's word in the forefront of
your thoughts. Review every action in light of them!

verses.zh: 也要教训你们的儿女，无论坐在家里，行在路上，躺下，起来，都要谈论；
verses.en: Teach them to your children and speak of them as you sit in your house, as you walk along the road,[NOTE:1] as you lie down, and as you get up.
notes: Or “as you are away on a journey” (cf. NRSV, TEV, NLT); NAB “at home and abroad.”
verses.commentary: 11:19 "teach them to your sons" This is a recurrent theme of Deuteronomy. See full note at Deut. 4:9.

verses.zh: 又要写在房屋的门框上，并城门上，
verses.en: Inscribe them on the doorframes of your houses and on your gates
verses.commentary:
11:20 "write" In the past some scholars have questioned the ability of Moses and the early Israelites to write. As
the archaeological evidence has grown, no one today would deny this. See "The Question of Israelite Literacy" in
Approaches to the Bible, vol. 2, pp. 142-53 (from Biblical Archaeology Society, 1995).

Here. it refers to the mezuza of Deut. 6:9, which was put on the front doorpost of the home. It contained
several texts from the Pentateuch.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

verses.zh: 使你们和你们子孙的日子在耶和华向你们列祖起誓、应许给他们的地上得以增多，如天覆地的日子那样多。
verses.en: so that your days and those of your descendants may be extended in the land that the Lord promised to give to your ancestors, like the days of heaven itself.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like the days of the heavens upon the earth,” that is, forever.
verses.commentary:
11:21

NASB
"as long as the heavens remain above the

earth"

NKJV
"like the days of the heavens are above the

earth"

NRSV
"as long as the heavens are above the earth"

TEV, NJB
"as long as there is sky above the earth"

Peshitta
"as the days of heaven upon earth"

JPSOA, LXX
"as long as there is a heaven over the earth"

This is a parallel statement to "perpetual ordinance" (e.g. Exod. 12:14,17,24,25; 13:10). This is
imagery of the permanence of the natural order. This is the basis of modern western scientific research..

verses.zh: 你们若留意谨守遵行我所吩咐这一切的诫命，爱耶和华―你们的　神，行他的道，专靠他，
verses.en: For if you carefully observe all of these commandments[NOTE:1] I am giving you[NOTE:2] and love the Lord your God, live according to his standards,[NOTE:3] and remain loyal to him,
notes: Heb “this commandment.” See note at Deut 5:30.
Heb “commanding you to do it.” For stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy, “giving” has been used in the translation and “to do it” has been left untranslated.
Heb “walk in all his ways” (so KJV, NIV84); NIV11 “walk in obedience to him”; TEV “do everything he commands.”
verses.commentary:
11:22 The conditional nature of the covenant (cf. Deut. 11:13; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT) and
its requirements are recurrent:

- the condition is similar to Deut. 11:13, but slightly different:

- "for if" and, BDB 49

- "to keep" BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT
VERB (grammatical construction used to bring emphasis; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- the requirements (series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS, like Deut. 11:13):

- "to do" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

- "to love" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17

- "to walk" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, cf. Deut. 8:6 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- "to hold fast to" ‒ BDB 179, KB 209, cf. Deut. 10:20; 13:4

verses.zh: 他必从你们面前赶出这一切国民，就是比你们更大更强的国民，你们也要得他们的地。
verses.en: then he[NOTE:1] will drive out all these nations ahead of you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
11:23-25 These are the promised results (i.e. "as He has spoken to you," Deut. 11:25) of the conditional covenant:

- "The Lord will drive out all the nations before you," Deut. 11:23, BDB 439, KB 441,
Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Exod. 34:24; Num. 32:21; Deut. 4:37-38; 9:4-5; Josh. 23:5,13

- "You will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you," Deut. 11:23, BDB 439, KB 441, Qal
PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 7:17; 9:3; Num. 33:52

- "Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours," Deut. 11:24, BDB 201, KB 231, Qal
IMPERFECT, cf Josh. 1:3. Their borders are described in Gen. 15:18; Exod. 23:31; Deut. 1:7; 3:12-17;
Josh. 1:1-4; 13:8-12

- "No man will be able to stand before you," Deut. 11:25, BDB 426, KB 427, Hithpael IMPERFECT,
cf. Deut. 7:24; Josh. 1:5; 10:8; 23:9

- "The Lord your God will lay," BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT

- "fear" ‒ BDB 808, cf. Deut. 2:25

- "dread" ‒ BDB 432, cf. Gen. 9:2

This same truth, but in different terms is in Exod. 23:27 and Josh. 2:9.

verses.zh: 凡你们脚掌所踏之地都必归你们；从旷野和黎巴嫩，并幼发拉底大河，直到西海，都要作你们的境界。
verses.en: Every place you set your foot[NOTE:1] will be yours; your border will extend from the desert to Lebanon and from the River (that is, the Euphrates) as far as the Mediterranean Sea.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the sole of your foot walks.” The placing of the foot symbolizes conquest and dominion, especially on land or on the necks of enemies (cf. Deut 1:36; Ps 7:13; Isa 63:3 Hab 3:19; Zech 9:13). See E. H. Merrill, NIDOTTE 1:992.
Heb “the after sea,” that is, the sea behind one when one is facing east, which is the normal OT orientation. Cf. ASV “the hinder sea.”
verses.commentary: 11:24 For full notes on the boundaries of the Promised Land see Deut. 1:8.

verses.zh: 必无一人能在你们面前站立得住；耶和华―你们的　神必照他所说的，使惧怕惊恐临到你们所踏之地的居民。
verses.en: Nobody will be able to resist you; the Lord your God will spread the fear and terror of you over the whole land on which you walk, just as he promised you.

verses.zh: 「看哪，我今日将祝福与咒诅的话都陈明在你们面前。
verses.en: Take note—I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:[NOTE:1]
notes: A blessing and a curse. Every extant treaty text of the late Bronze Age attests to a section known as the “blessings and curses,” the former for covenant loyalty and the latter for covenant breach. Blessings were promised rewards for obedience; curses were threatened judgments for disobedience. In the Book of Deuteronomy these are fully developed in 27:1-28:68. Here Moses adumbrates the whole by way of anticipation.
verses.commentary:
11:26-28 These verses continue the consequences of the conditional covenant between YHWH and
His people. They are expanded in Deuteronomy 27-29 (cf. Leviticus 26). These verses explain much of the history of the Jews.

This paragraph starts out with a common call for attention, "See" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal
IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 1:8,21; 2:24; 4:5; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39. The term "today" (BDB 398) is a way of
urging decisive, immediate action (cf. Deut. 4:39).

- "blessing" ‒ BDB 139

- "if you listen" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT, "hear so as to do,"
cf. commanded in Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:10; 33:7; conditioned in Deut. 7:12; 11:13 (twice);
15:5 (twice); 28:1(twice),13; 30:10,17

- "curse" ‒ BDB 887

- "if you do not listen," same as above, Qal IMPERFECT

- "turn aside" ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT with waw

- "following other gods" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, literally, "walking," cf. Deut. 6:14; 8:19; 11:28;
13:2; 28:14; Jdg. 2:12; Jer. 7:6,9; 11:10; 13:10

This contrast of destinies is often called "the two ways" (cf. Deut. 28 and 30:1,15-20; Ps. 1; Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14).

▣ "a blessing" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

verses.zh: 你们若听从耶和华―你们　神的诫命，就是我今日所吩咐你们的，就必蒙福。
verses.en: the blessing if you take to heart[NOTE:1] the commandments of the Lord your God that I am giving you today,
notes: Heb “listen to,” that is, obey.

verses.zh: 你们若不听从耶和华―你们　神的诫命，偏离我今日所吩咐你们的道，去事奉你们素来所不认识的别神，就必受祸。
verses.en: and the curse if you pay no attention[NOTE:1] to his[NOTE:2] commandments and turn from the way I am setting before[NOTE:3] you today to pursue[NOTE:4] other gods you have not known.
notes: Heb “do not listen to,” that is, do not obey.
Heb “the commandments of the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “am commanding” (so NASB, NRSV).
Heb “walk after”; NIV “by following”; NLT “by worshiping.” This is a violation of the first commandment, the most serious of the covenant violations (Deut 5:6-7).
verses.commentary: 11:28 "which you have not known" This is literally "know." See full note at Deut. 4:35 and SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW.

verses.zh: 及至耶和华―你的　神领你进入要去得为业的那地，你就要将祝福的话陈明在基利心山上，将咒诅的话陈明在以巴路山上。
verses.en: When the Lord your God brings you into the land you are to possess, you must pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.[NOTE:1]
notes: Mount Gerizim…Mount Ebal. These two mountains are near the ancient site of Shechem and the modern city of Nablus. The valley between them is like a great amphitheater with the mountain slopes as seating sections. The place was sacred because it was there that Abraham pitched his camp and built his first altar after coming to Canaan (Gen 12:6). Jacob also settled at Shechem for a time and dug a well from which Jesus once requested a drink of water (Gen 33:18-20; John 4:5-7). When Joshua and the Israelites finally brought Canaan under control they assembled at Shechem as Moses commanded and undertook a ritual of covenant reaffirmation (Josh 8:30-35; 24:1, 25). Half the tribes stood on Mt. Gerizim and half on Mt. Ebal and in antiphonal chorus pledged their loyalty to the Lord before Joshua and the Levites who stood in the valley below (Josh 8:33; cf. Deut 27:11-13).
verses.commentary:
11:29 "the blessing. . .the curse" This verse describes the covenant renewal ceremony conducted
by Joshua at Shechem (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28 and Josh. 8:30-35). Apparently two groups of Levitical singers sang
or chanted the blessing from Mt. Gerezim and the curses from Mr. Ebal. These two mountains flank Shechem
(i.e. meaning shoulder blades, BDB 1014). Archaeology has found a large stone altar on Mt. Ebal which matches
the description of this altar in the Talmud. See Introduction to the book VII.

This follows the Suzerain Hittite Treaties, which relate to the king and his vassal subjects
(cf. Deuteronomy 27; Joshua 24 for the same pattern).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

verses.zh: 这二山岂不是在约旦河那边，日落之处，在住亚拉巴的迦南人之地与吉甲相对，靠近摩利橡树吗？
verses.en: Are they not across the Jordan River,[NOTE:1] toward the west, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the rift valley opposite Gilgal[NOTE:2] near the oak[NOTE:3] of Moreh?
notes: The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

Gilgal. From a Hebrew verb root גָּלַל (galal, “to roll”) this place name means “circle” or “rolling,” a name given because God had “rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you” (Josh 5:9). It is perhaps to be identified with Khirbet el-Metjir, 1.2 mi (2 km) northeast of OT Jericho.

The MT plural “oaks” (אֵלוֹנֵי, ʾeloney) should probably be altered (with many Greek texts) to the singular “oak” (אֵלוֹן, ʾelon; cf. NRSV) in line with the only other occurrence of the phrase (Gen 12:6). The Syriac, Tg. Ps.-J. read mmrʾ, confusing this place with the “oaks of Mamre” near Hebron (Gen 13:18). Smr also appears to confuse “Moreh” with “Mamre” (reading mwrʾ, a combined form), adding the clarification mwl shkm (“near Shechem”) apparently to distinguish it from Mamre near Hebron.
verses.commentary:
11:30 "Arabah" This is the Jordan Valley south of the Dead Sea. See note at Deut. 1:1.

▣ "Gilgal" This means a "circle of stones" (BDB 166 II), which was the name of the Israelites' first
camp site in Canaan (cf. Josh. 4:19). However, this one is farther north near Shechem (see The IVP Bible
Background Commentary, OT, p. 181). See full note at Gen. 13:18 online at
www.freebiblecommentary.org.

▣ "oaks of Moreh" This was a sacred tree or grove near Shechem (cf. Gen. 12:6 and 35:4). The UBS
Text Project, p. 281, gives the PLURAL "oaks" an "A" rating (high probability).

Moreh means "teacher" (BDB 435).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

verses.zh: 你们要过约旦河，进去得耶和华―你们　神所赐你们为业之地，在那地居住。
verses.en: For you are about to cross the Jordan to possess the land the Lord your God is giving you, and you will possess and inhabit it.
verses.commentary:
11:31-32 These are summary verses recounting what has been stated many times before.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why does Deuteronomy repeat the same phrases and historical incidents so much?

- How are the conditional or volitional elements of the Covenant emphasized?

- How is the sovereignty of YHWH emphasized?

verses.en: Be certain to keep all the statutes and ordinances that I am presenting to you today.
